title: Viv's ChatGPT sales jumped 436% | GEO
description: Period care brand Viv saw sales from ChatGPT recommendations jump 436%. Here is what it had published that AI tools picked up.
h1: Viv saw sales from ChatGPT recommendations jump 436%
intro: Period care brand Viv told Modern Retail that many shoppers ChatGPT sent to its blog went on to buy. Sales from those picks jumped 436%. The brand also says Google's AI helped it sell about six months of tampon stock in three weeks.

keyNumbers.label: jump in sales from ChatGPT recommendations
spike in monthly traffic in July 2024, driven mainly by Gemini and ChatGPT
to sell out about six months of tampon stock

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: In July 2024 Viv's monthly traffic spiked by 400%. Marketing and design director Kelly Donohue said it came out of nowhere. When she dug in, she found most of it came from Google Gemini and ChatGPT recommending non-toxic period care.

The timing mattered. A study in the journal Environment International had just found metals like lead and arsenic in many popular tampon brands. People asked AI about toxins in tampons, and the answers sent them to Viv's blog. Many of those visitors bought.

sections.heading: What Viv had published
paragraphs: Right after the study came out, Viv posted an article titled "Lead & Arsenic in Tampons?! Here's Why Viv is Your Safest Tampon Choice." Donohue said it was the brand's top converting post of 2024.

Viv's website and social posts explain in detail how its products are made, how safe the ingredients are and how they're tested. The brand also put its safety standards at the centre of its email, SMS and social media. Donohue thinks having facts about the brand in lots of places helped AI tools find it.

sections.heading: The Google side
paragraphs: The effect carried on in the months that followed. Donohue says Google's AI picks helped sell out tampon stock that was meant to last about six months.

quotes.text: We ended up selling out of about six months of tampon inventory in three weeks, driven by Google's AI-powered recommendations.
quotes.who: Kelly Donohue, marketing and design director at Viv

quotes.text: These AI tools are specifically scraping through content, but looking for more than just keywords.
quotes.who: Kelly Donohue, marketing and design director at Viv

lessons: Answer the question people are asking right now. Viv posted its article on lead and arsenic in tampons as soon as the study made news. It became the brand's best-selling post of 2024.
Go into detail. Viv explains how it makes, checks and tests its products. Donohue says that's the kind of detail AI tools look for when they build an answer.
Say the same thing everywhere. Viv carried its safety message across its blog, email, SMS and social media.
caveat: The 436% figure is Modern Retail's summary of Viv's results. The article does not give the sales figure it grew from.

source.title: Brands are seeing an influx of traffic from ChatGPT and Google Gemini
source.author: Gabriela Barkho

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: Draco Diamond sells lab-grown diamond jewellery online, made to order. In spring 2026, founder Garrett McMartin focused on getting the brand to show up in AI answers. Afterwards, AI tools made up 5.45% of the site's traffic, up from 0.18% before. In May and July, AI's share of sessions reached 7.3% and 6.6%.
ChatGPT alone accounts for 84% of the store's AI referral traffic. Over the same period, the traffic mix shifted away from paid ads toward organic search and AI.

sections.heading: How AI shoppers behave
paragraphs: McMartin said shoppers from AI add things to their cart five times as often as visitors from Google Ads. That's more than double the site average. They also stay on the site 20% longer. sections.heading: Revenue, with a caution
paragraphs: In April and May 2026, revenue was up 5% and 10% on the same months a year earlier. In June and July, after the push was done, it grew 78% and 195%. The article is careful to say McMartin only saw the two happen together. So it doesn't show the AI work caused the jump.

quotes.text: It seems that a lot of our AI traffic is at the end of that research funnel, and they're almost ready to buy, so that's why we're getting such a high add to cart from these users.
quotes.who: Garrett McMartin, founder of Draco Diamond

lessons: Measure AI as its own channel. McMartin tracked AI's share of sessions month by month, which is how he could see it move from 0.18% to 5.45%.
Expect shoppers who are still deciding. Many of Draco's AI visitors look around, leave and come back later to buy. So the first visit often isn't the sale.
Look past traffic. AI visitors were Draco's highest-intent group, adding to cart five times as often as Google Ads visitors.
caveat: As the article says, the founder only noticed sales rising at the same time. It does not prove the AI work caused it.

sections.heading: The numbers
paragraphs: La Joya Jewelry sells lab-grown diamonds online. At the start of 2026, about 2% to 3% of its referral traffic came from AI sources. By early September it was about 5% or 6%.
Mehta said these visitors buy far more often than others. For example, he said that if 3% of shoppers normally buy, more than 13% of shoppers from AI do.

sections.heading: Why he thinks it works
paragraphs: Mehta's view is that a recommendation carries trust. A shopper who has been told a company is good is more likely to believe it. He also said the biggest trend is that these shoppers have already done their research.

paragraphs: AI shoppers don't always spend more. Mehta said he hasn't seen them spend more than other customers. He said jewellery buyers usually come with a budget in mind.

AI shoppers arrive informed. La Joya's visitors from AI have usually done their research, so they need less convincing on the basics.

h1: One ChatGPT question brought Hingees an order of over ₦250,000
intro: Nigerian lifestyle brand Hingees got a first order of over ₦250,000 from a new shopper, TechCabal reported. The shopper had asked ChatGPT for Nigerian leather brands. It is one order, not a trend, but it surprised the founder.

keyNumbers.label: spent by one first-time buyer who found Hingees through ChatGPT

sections.heading: The order
paragraphs: Hingees sells leather goods and clothing. First-time buyers usually start small, with a shirt or maybe a notebook. So when a new customer ordered over ₦250,000 of leather goods, it looked like it might be fraud. Someone from the team called to check.
The order was real. The customer explained she had not found Hingees through Instagram ads, Google search or a friend. She had asked ChatGPT for Nigerian leather brands, and Hingees showed up.

sections.heading: The groundwork behind it
paragraphs: Founder Hammed Okunade says Hingees is obsessed with tidy product details, tagged photos and smart keywords. It did that work for years to show up in Google. TechCabal's point is that AI now helps shoppers look, compare and decide in one chat. That earlier work is what AI can read.
The article says a small brand with good product details and photos can show up next to big brands without paying for ads. Sellers who only use Instagram or WhatsApp may be invisible to AI tools.

quotes.text: I always thought large orders came from returning customers or ads, and they still do. I just never imagined a chatbot would also be bringing us customers.

lessons: Clean product details keep paying off. Okunade spent years on tidy product details, tagged photos and keywords. TechCabal says that's the kind of information AI tools can read.
Small brands can appear next to big ones. TechCabal says good product details and photos can get a small store picked without paying for ads.
Find out how new buyers found you. Hingees only found out about ChatGPT because the customer said so on the phone call.
caveat: This is a single order. It shows what can happen, not what usually happens.

title: SteelSeries: AI search revenue grew 3.7X | GEO
description: Gaming brand SteelSeries and its agency report traffic from AI search up 23X and revenue from AI search platforms up 3.7X.
h1: SteelSeries grew revenue from AI search platforms 3.7X
intro: Gaming gear brand SteelSeries and its agency, NoGood, ran a ten-month program. They say visits from AI search grew 23X on the year before. Sales from those visits grew 27X, and money from AI search grew 3.7X. The figures come from an award-winning case study published by The Drum.

keyNumbers.label: more visits from AI search than the year before
growth in conversions from those visitors
growth in revenue from AI search platforms

sections.heading: What they found first
paragraphs: Early research showed that only a few sources shaped AI's picks for gaming gear. There were a handful of review sites and a group of Reddit threads. So to get picked, SteelSeries had to earn reviews and trust online, not just improve its own site.

sections.heading: What they changed
paragraphs: Product pages were rebuilt with short answers near the top, questions and answers, and simple tables that AI tools can quote. Product data code was added across the site. Problems that stopped bots from reading pages were fixed.

The team contacted the exact sites and reviewers that shape AI answers about gaming gear. Old reviews were swapped for new mentions. On Reddit, the team joined the exact threads AI was quoting, with truly useful posts instead of ads. Product feeds were also prepared for ChatGPT Shopping, Amazon Rufus and Google AI Mode shopping.

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: Traffic from AI search platforms grew 23X year over year, reaching more than 1,500 daily visitors by October 2025. Sales from those visitors grew 27X, and they bought more often than people from normal search. Money from AI search grew 3.7X. By the end, SteelSeries held the top spot for gaming headsets, keyboards and earbuds on Gemini, ChatGPT and Perplexity.

lessons: Find the sources AI trusts in your category. For SteelSeries it was a few review sites and Reddit threads, so that is where the effort went.
Make product pages easy to quote. Short answers up top, question and answer sections and clear tables give AI tools clean text to use.
Check nothing is blocking crawlers. Fixing pages that crawlers could not read was part of the work.
Join conversations honestly. The team added useful posts to the Reddit threads AI cited, not brand promotion.
caveat: These numbers come from the agency's own award entry, not from a news report. NoGood's own case study page gives different numbers in its text (6.7X more visits and 7.1X more sales). So treat them with care.

sections.heading: Where Levenger started

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The agency worked on three things. It fixed the site so AI tools could read it and quote it correctly. It wrote clearer guides about the products. Picture the exact question. The work was judged by whether Levenger would come up when someone asked ChatGPT for products for serious writers.
Value per visitor matters more than volume. A small number of AI visitors can count when each is worth $92 against a $6 average.

title: Ahrefs: 12.1% of sign-ups from AI search | GEO
description: At Ahrefs, visitors from AI search were 0.5% of traffic but brought 12.1% of sign-ups, converting 23 times better than Google visitors.
h1: At Ahrefs, 0.5% of visitors brought 12.1% of sign-ups
intro: Marketing software company Ahrefs looked at 30 days of visits. Visitors from AI search were just 0.5% of them, but they brought 12.1% of its sign-ups. By its numbers, AI search visitors were 23 times more likely to sign up than visitors from normal Google search.

keyNumbers.label: of Ahrefs' traffic came from AI search over the last 30 days
of sign-ups came from AI search in the same period
more likely to sign up than visitors from normal search

sections.heading: What Ahrefs measured
paragraphs: Patrick Stox looked at Ahrefs' own website data. He counted AI search as visits from assistants like ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini. Over the last 30 days they made up 0.5% of traffic, and 0.3% for the year to date. Most of that traffic came from ChatGPT, and so did the vast majority of the sign-ups.
Even so, those visitors made 12.1% of all sign-ups. So AI search got Ahrefs more sign-ups per visit than any other source.

sections.heading: Not all good news
paragraphs: Other measures were mixed. Fewer AI visitors left straight away and they viewed 50% more pages, but they spent less time on the site. Stox also made a rough guess that people in AI search click links 75% less than in normal search. He wasn't sure the higher sign-up rate would grow enough to make up for it.

quotes.text: That's crazy right? 12.1% of signups from 0.5% of the traffic. This channel performs really well for us.
quotes.who: Patrick Stox, Technical SEO at Ahrefs when he wrote the post

lessons: Judge AI by results, not visits. A tiny slice of traffic produced an outsized share of sign-ups.
Check where AI visitors land. Ahrefs found most went to its home page, free tools and product pages, so those pages need to be ready.
Expect fewer clicks overall. If people click less in AI answers, each visit you do get counts for more.
caveat: This is one software company's 30-day snapshot. Ahrefs sells subscriptions, not products, and sign-ups are not sales.

source.title: Does AI Search Traffic Convert Better Than Traditional Search? For Ahrefs, Yes: 0.5% of Visitors Drove 12.1% of Signups

title: Webflow: 10% of sign-ups from AI tools | GEO
description: Webflow gets 10% of sign-ups from AI tools, up 4x in a year, and ChatGPT visitors convert at 24%. What its growth team learned.
h1: Webflow now gets 10% of its sign-ups from AI tools
intro: Website builder Webflow gets 10% of its sign-ups from people who found it through AI. That's 4x more than a year before. The numbers come from its VP of Growth, Josh Grant, in Kyle Poyar's Growth Unhinged newsletter. Visitors from ChatGPT convert at 24%, six times the rate of Google.

keyNumbers.label: of Webflow's sign-ups come from AI discovery, up 4x year on year
conversion rate for traffic from ChatGPT, 6x higher than Google
of Webflow's AI referrals come from ChatGPT alone

sections.heading: The numbers
paragraphs: Webflow is a website building company with about 300,000 customers. 10% of its sign-ups now come from AI tools, 4x more than a year before. The newsletter says the real effect is likely bigger than this number.

91% of those AI referrals come from ChatGPT, followed by Perplexity (4%), Copilot (2%), Gemini (2%) and Claude (1%). ChatGPT traffic converts at 24%, six times Google's rate, and two in three AI-referred conversions happen within seven days.

sections.heading: What Webflow learned
paragraphs: Total visits can fool you. Webflow's less useful visits fell, while its better visits grew. AI answers also change all the time, so showing up one day doesn't mean you'll show up the next.

The team tracks three things. How often Webflow shows up in AI answers. How well AI tools describe it next to rivals. And how many sign-ups come from AI. It tried an llms.txt file and saw no significant lift. It also sees Reddit as important, and answers real questions there instead of just posting links.

quotes.text: A lot of our lower value and lower intent traffic has gone down, but there's higher quality traffic occurring even as the aggregate declines.
quotes.who: Josh Grant, VP of Growth at Webflow

quotes.text: When I say AI engines are volatile, I mean it's not like Google where you rank once and hold it.
quotes.who: Josh Grant, VP of Growth at Webflow

lessons: Don't judge by total traffic. Webflow's weaker visits fell while better ones grew.
Check what AI says about you. Webflow checks how different AI apps describe it next to rivals, and fixes what's wrong.
Skip the shortcuts. Webflow saw no significant lift from an llms.txt file and focuses on content instead.
Be useful on Reddit. Webflow answers the questions people really ask, instead of posting links.
caveat: Webflow sells software, not products, and sign-ups are not sales. The rest of the newsletter post is for paid subscribers.

h1: ChatGPT now refers around 10% of Vercel's new sign-ups
intro: Vercel, a platform for software makers, says ChatGPT now sends about 10% of its new sign-ups. That's up from 4.8% the month before and 1% six months earlier. The figure comes from a June 2025 post on Vercel's own blog.

keyNumbers.label: of new Vercel sign-ups now referred by ChatGPT (around)

sections.heading: The shift
paragraphs: Vercel's post starts with a simple point. AI tools now answer many questions right away, often with no click at all. Even so, ChatGPT went from referring 1% of Vercel's new sign-ups to around 10% in six months. The post also points to research that says Google's AI Overviews may cut clicks by up to 34.5%, against similar searches without one.

sections.heading: How Vercel adapted
paragraphs: Vercel kept doing traditional search work and added to it. Its advice is to give the clearest and fullest explanation of a topic. Use your own data and examples that others can't easily copy. Pages should have clear headings and data code. They shouldn't need JavaScript, because most AI bots read pages but don't run it.

It also says to earn real mentions in online groups and not to pay for links. Check your pages after 30, 90 and 180 days so they stay correct. To track results, it suggests watching citations in AI answers and visits from sites such as chat.openai.com and perplexity.ai.

quotes.text: Search isn't just about ranking anymore. It's about being surfaced in new places, under new rules.

lessons: Make sure pages work without JavaScript. Vercel notes most AI crawlers read pages but do not run JavaScript.
Be the clearest answer. Vercel says AI tools like the clearest, fullest explanation, not the page that repeats a keyword the most.
Keep content fresh. Vercel reviews pages at 30, 90 and 180 days, because stale pages get used less.
caveat: Vercel is a software company, and the figure is for sign-ups, not sales.

sections.heading: 2025: ChatGPT moves to the top
paragraphs: Tally has always grown through word of mouth and organic search. In a June 2025 post, the team wrote that ChatGPT now sent it more visitors than any other site. lessons: Be present where people talk. Tally credits years of honest answers and sharing in forums and on Reddit, which AI tools now read.

title: Joe & Bella: holiday sales from ChatGPT | GEO
description: Adaptive clothing brand Joe & Bella saw new customers arrive from ChatGPT, and some bought over the holidays. What the brand thinks helped.
h1: ChatGPT sent Joe & Bella new customers who bought over the holidays
intro: Clothing brand Joe & Bella saw a wave of new customers come from ChatGPT, Modern Retail reported. Some of them bought during the 2024 holidays. The article gives no sales figures.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Joe & Bella sells clothes that are easier to put on for older people and people with illnesses like Parkinson's. In the months before the article, a wave of new customers came to its website from ChatGPT. Some of them bought over the holidays.
Co-founder and CEO Jimmy Zollo admitted he did not know what those shoppers had asked ChatGPT to find the brand.

sections.heading: What the brand thinks helped
paragraphs: Zollo's theory is that the search keywords the brand keeps investing in, and its blog, are the likely reasons. Its search ads often use terms such as "adaptive clothing".
Joe & Bella planned to keep writing about how its clothes work, using words that AI chatbots can pick up.

quotes.text: I don't really know how or what they would have typed or asked ChatGPT to have found us over the holidays.
quotes.who: Jimmy Zollo, co-founder and CEO of Joe & Bella

quotes.text: It was pretty cool and unexpected, but we need to better understand how to optimize for these searches going forward.
quotes.who: Jimmy Zollo, co-founder and CEO of Joe & Bella

lessons: Steady content work can surface in AI answers. Zollo believes the brand's ongoing keyword work and blog are why ChatGPT found it.
Explain what makes your products different. Joe & Bella planned more content about its products' technology for AI chatbots to pick up.
You may never see the question. Even the CEO did not know what shoppers typed into ChatGPT before they arrived.
caveat: The article gives no numbers. It shows that shoppers from ChatGPT bought, not how many or how much.

source.title: Brands are seeing an influx of traffic from ChatGPT and Google Gemini
source.author: Gabriela Barkho

cardHeadline: Visits from AI up 2,434% over Black Friday and Cyber Monday
title: JBL: AI referrals up 2,434% at Black Friday | GEO
description: Audio brand JBL saw referrals from AI tools rise 2,434% over Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025 after rethinking its content for AI.
h1: JBL's referrals from AI tools rose 2,434% over Black Friday
intro: Audio brand JBL worked with the agency Code and Theory. Visits from AI tools rose 2,434% over Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025, by numbers the two shared with Marketing Brew. The article reports visits, not sales.

keyNumbers.label: rise in referrals from AI tools over Black Friday and Cyber Monday
more engagement on four YouTube Shorts made for search, against JBL's 30-day average

sections.heading: What JBL changed
paragraphs: JBL worked with Code and Theory to check how it showed up in search and rethink its website. They also planned stories that work for both people and bots. The stories try to be fun to read and clear about features. They answer everyday questions, like whether a soundbar is really worth buying.

For Black Friday, JBL published a gift guide showing which of its products suit different kinds of gift recipients. The team also studied how people search on YouTube and TikTok. Then it made short videos to match, like a YouTube Short comparing two speakers.

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: Across Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025, referrals from AI tools were up 2,434%. Four YouTube Shorts made for search got a 2.61% engagement rate per view. The agency says that's 200x JBL's 30-day average of 0.013%.
The agency said the work was slow and steady, not an overnight win. JBL is still working out how to use it in other countries.

quotes.text: We wanted to identify what was the best strategy for JBL, and not just a generic strategy for SEO.
quotes.who: Carolina González, manager, global digital content strategy at JBL

quotes.text: The way that we see it, search is everywhere now. But that doesn't mean that people search the same way on every platform.
quotes.who: Bryn Dodson, creative director, copy, at Code and Theory (JBL's agency)

lessons: Answer the doubts buyers have. JBL writes around everyday questions, like whether a soundbar is worth buying.
Let your gift guide do the matching. JBL's Black Friday guide said which products suit which kind of recipient.
Treat it as a long game. JBL's agency calls this slow and steady work, not overnight growth.
caveat: The press article confirms the jump in referrals only. JBL's award entry also claims "10x more revenue than the next highest period". It doesn't say what that money covers, so we don't count it as a sales result.

source.title: 'Search is everywhere': How JBL is retooling its search efforts for AI
source.author: Kristina Monllos

cardHeadline: Sales from AI up 78%, mostly from ChatGPT
title: RAVE Coffee: AI-referred sales up 78% | GEO
description: An agency reports a 78% rise in sales attributed to AI referrals for UK roaster RAVE Coffee, with ChatGPT behind over 95% of them.
h1: RAVE Coffee's agency reports a 78% rise in AI-referred sales
intro: UK agency The SEO Works reports a 78% rise in sales from AI visits for a coffee brand. The case study shows the RAVE Coffee logo. ChatGPT accounted for more than 95% of those AI-driven transactions.

keyNumbers.label: rise in sales from AI visits
of AI-driven transactions came from ChatGPT
more sales that AI helped with, against the year before

sections.heading: What the agency did
paragraphs: The SEO Works checked the site and listed what shoppers were looking for. Then it split each product, category and guide page into clear blocks that AI tools and search engines can use as answers. It showed more of what the brand knows, like product facts, where the coffee comes from and real experience. It also added a page for the brand's café.

It also checked the site's data code, with a plan to add FAQs and product details. It linked brewing guides, blends and how-to pages together. And it suggested ways to get the brand mentioned more in forums. Special tracking split out visits from AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini. So the brand could see its sales from AI for the first time.

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: Within twelve months, visits from AI grew from a few to a steady stream, with a 91% engagement rate. AI-assisted conversions rose 36.5% year on year, site searches rose 182% and product quiz completions rose 247%.

Sales directly attributed to AI referrals rose 78%, and ChatGPT made up more than 95% of AI-driven transactions. AI shoppers often bought pricier things like espresso machines, gift subscriptions and brewing gear. The brand's best-known blend became the top product from AI, with sales up 900% on the year before.

lessons: Break pages into clear answers. The agency split product and guide pages into blocks that AI tools can quote.
Show where your products come from. Origin details and real expertise were added to build trust.
Track AI on its own. Special tracking let the brand see AI visits, orders and sales apart from normal search for the first time.
caveat: This is an agency case study we rate low on trust. The brand only shows up as a logo, and the text says "this leading coffee brand". The 78% has no starting number, and no one at the brand is quoted.

cardHeadline: AI shoppers spend $5.50 more per order but buy less often
title: Edible: AI shoppers spend more, convert less | GEO
description: At gifting retailer Edible Brands, orders from AI shoppers are $5.50 bigger than average, but they convert below the site's usual rate.
h1: At Edible Brands, AI shoppers spend more but convert less
intro: Gift shop Edible Brands told Digital Commerce 360 that orders from AI visitors are $5.50 bigger than its site average. But those visitors convert at more than 5%, below the site's usual rate of more than 10%.

keyNumbers.label: bigger average order from AI visitors than the site average
conversion rate from AI traffic, below a site average of more than 10%
of AI referral traffic comes from ChatGPT (about)

sections.heading: The good part
paragraphs: Edible Brands is a large US gifting retailer, No. 182 in the Digital Commerce 360 Top 1000. Chief digital officer Erica Randerson said AI is still a small part of its visits, less than 10%. ChatGPT brings about 95% of those.
Those shoppers spend more. The average order from AI visitors is $5.50 more than the site average. Randerson said AI visitors seem a little less drawn to cheaper goods.

sections.heading: The less good part
paragraphs: AI visitors convert at more than 5%, which Randerson called strong. But it is lower than Edible's site average of more than 10%. She said that's because of the kind of store Edible is. People come to buy a gift, and they usually know who it's for.

quotes.text: But I will say: That's lower than our site average.
quotes.who: Erica Randerson, chief digital officer at Edible Brands

quotes.text: We have a high intent audience. They're coming in knowing who they're shopping for most of the time.
quotes.who: Erica Randerson, chief digital officer at Edible Brands

lessons: Compare AI shoppers with your own average. At Edible they looked strong on their own but converted below the site's usual rate.
Know your baseline. Edible's usual shoppers already come with a clear goal. That's why so many of them buy.
Look at order value too. Even with lower conversion, Edible's AI orders were $5.50 bigger on average.
caveat: A mixed result: AI shoppers spend a little more per order but convert below the site's usual rate. Results like this vary from store to store.

source.title: How AI referrals are impacting traffic at 4 online retailers
source.author: Abbas Haleem
